title: Google's AI flood forecasts reach Nigeria: warnings days ahead and cash before the water rises

claims.text: Google says its AI predicts river floods up to seven days before they strike and urban flash floods up to 24 hours before they hit.
claims.label: Flash-flood warning time

claims.text: Google says its flood forecasting now covers areas across 150 countries where more than 2 billion people live.
claims.label: Countries covered

claims.text: The forecasts are available through Flood Hub and also appear in Google Search when people look for information on a flood in their area.
For urban flash floods, Google built a method called Groundsource, which uses its Gemini AI to analyse historical news reports.
Google says Groundsource reviewed more than 5 million reports spanning roughly 20 years and helped create a dataset of about 2.6 million flood events.
In Kogi, Nigeria, one of West Africa's most flood-affected regions, GiveDirectly used Google's Flood Forecasting API to deliver cash to people before the water rose.
Google says GiveDirectly found that the early cash helped families evacuate, protect assets and rebuild.
Urban flash flooding was the hard problem because sensors almost never monitor it, according to Streamline Feed.

Flood Hub uses two integrated AI models: a hydrologic model that forecasts the amount of water flowing in a river, and an inundation model that predicts which areas will be affected and to what depth.
Google says the Groundsource method helps forecast floods in areas that lack local sensors.
Researchers can access the predictions through Flood Hub, and can use open-source data and an API for their own disaster resilience research.
